notes: Partition verified: 48 source ids (one two-morpheme unit) and all 51 target ids accounted for once.
*Is there never* divides as rule 50's interrogative existential directs: `הֲ` takes the fronted *Is*, `אַיִן` keeps *there never* headed on the negation word.

`בְעֵינַי` → *well* is retained as a two-morpheme fusion: one English word carries both preposition and construct noun, neither owns a part of it (rules 30, 40), and it heads on `עַיִן` under rule 23; the competing reading would leave the preposition `unrepresented` beside the noun.
The single written *the* of *the uncircumcised Philistines* goes to the one article morpheme in the phrase, which stands on the adjective (rule 47).
